blog_summary: Adrian Colyer reflects on David Parnas' 1995 essay, which was awarded ICSE's 'Most Influential Paper' recognition. Parnas argues that while academic papers often claim influence, most practicing programmers neither read nor apply research findings. He attributes this gap to academia's failure to produce 'how-to' papers that explain foundational assumptions and practical guidance, instead focusing on 'this is what I did' comparisons. The blog post highlights Parnas' critique of the research community's disconnect with industry, noting that practitioners need accessible, assumption-driven explanations rather than technical novelty. Colyer adds his perspective, acknowledging the vast volume of research but observing strengthening ties between academia and industry, particularly in data and distributed systems, with examples like UC Berkeley's AMPLab and Jonas Boner's work on Akka Cluster.
